program_name: Master in Computing for Data Science
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH — 100%, with no Italian or German component at any point. The official study plan states unambiguously under the heading 'Teaching language': 'The official language of the Master's programme is English.' The admission-information PDF repeats: 'The official teaching language is English.' Every course in both curricula is delivered in English, including the 3 CP 'Advanced English for Scientific Communication' (a pass/fail academic-writing course, not a foreign-language course) and the 24 CP thesis. Unlike the trilingual unibz bachelor programmes, there is NO second or third teaching language, no Italian/German course embedded in the plan, and no language-position system. This is the single most important structural difference from the sister Bachelor in Computer Science at the same faculty, which is trilingual and effectively closed to English-only applicants.
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano — the university's technology-park campus at Bruno-Buozzi-Straße 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Faculty of Engineering. This is a separate site from the main Bolzano city-centre campus (Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1), where the Advisory Service sits, and from the Brixen-Bressanone and Bruneck-Brunico campuses. All teaching for this programme is at NOI Techpark.
degree_class: LM-18 (Informatica / Computer Science). 120 ECTS over 2 years (4 semesters). Notable professional consequence stated on the programme page: graduates of LM-18 are eligible to sit the Italian State Examination for admission to the profession of 'Ingegnere dell'informazione' and, after passing, may register in Section A (Information Engineering) of the professional register of engineers.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and confirmed running. The programme page carries the status line 'Courses will definetely be starting' (unibz's own spelling). Both the Early Bird and the Late ranking lists for a.y. 2026/27 have already been published and signed, confirming the intake actually ran and places were filled. Beyond that, the Additional Application Session for 2026/27 is CURRENTLY OPEN for this programme: the official Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Computing for Data Science' as '(Application possible)', with the window running 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 (noon). As of the verification date 2026-08-29 this window is still open, but it is restricted to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment.
is_new_programme: No — not a new programme, but a RESTRUCTURED and RENAMED one, which is why it is easy to mistake for new. The Faculty's own study-guide page states: 'If you enroled before 2021/22, you are enroled in our previous Master in Computer Science or in a previous version of our Master in Computational Data Science', and advises those students: 'we strongly encourage you to switch to our Master in Computing for Data Science: previous exams will be recognised as favourably as possible.' So the current Master in Computing for Data Science took its present form for cohorts from 2021/22 and is the successor to BOTH the discontinued Master in Computer Science (whose old study manifestos, 'Manifest-2013-msc-CS_en.pdf' through 'Manifest-2017-msc-CS_en.pdf', are still archived on the study-plan page) and the earlier Master in Computational Data Science. The study plan has been revised again for cohorts from 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26. This corroborates the researcher's working note that the programme stands in place of the closed MSc Computer Science, though unibz never uses the word 'closed' — it frames it as a migration path.
majors_tracks_study_plans: Two curricula (unibz calls them both 'curricula' and, in the brochure, 'majors'); students share a common compulsory core and then specialise. (1) MACHINE LEARNING — oriented toward data-driven AI and machine-learning methods for data analysis, data exploration, interpretation and visualisation of results, and knowledge extraction to guide decision-making. Compulsory beyond the core: Natural Language Processing and Recommender Systems (6), Machine Learning (6), Deep Learning (6), Large Language Models and Information Retrieval (6). (2) ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DATA MANAGEMENT — focused on data management and on AI techniques for building IT architectures, infrastructures and systems for storing, maintaining, integrating and curating complex heterogeneous data. Compulsory beyond the core: Data Semantics (6), Process Mining (6), Data Curation (12 = Data Preparation and Integration 6 + Data Profiling 6). SHARED CORE (both curricula, year 1 semester 1, 30 CP): Algorithms and Data Management for Artificial Intelligence (12 = Data Management and Business Intelligence 6 + Algorithms for Artificial Intelligence 6), Mathematics and Statistics for Data Science (6), Programming and Visualisation for Data Science (12 = Programming in Python 6 + Data Analysis and Visualization 6). SHARED LATER: Capstone Project (6, pass/fail), Advanced English for Scientific Communication (3, pass/fail), Legal and Ethical Aspects of Artificial Intelligence (3, pass/fail), Thesis (24). CUSTOMISATION: 18 CP of curriculum-specific optional courses (three 6 CP choices) plus 12 CP of Free Choice courses or internships. Optional-course pool includes Advanced Statistics, Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Cloud Computing and Distributed Systems, Computer Vision, Data Curation, Data Semantics, Parallel Computing, Process Mining, Real-Time Big Data Processing, Time Series Analysis (the pool differs slightly per curriculum — each curriculum's compulsory courses appear as options for the other). TIMING RULE: the curriculum must be chosen by the end of the first semester of year 1; changes are possible within the first year, using the 'Change of Curriculum' form, approved by the Tutor and the Degree Course Committee. A student may also leave the curriculum structure entirely and move to an approved Individual Study Plan, modifiable twice a year (October-November and March-April). Part-time enrolment is available. There is no dual-study or four-year variant.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — fully and genuinely open to a candidate who speaks only English. This is the decisive finding and it is the exact opposite of the sister Bachelor in Computer Science. Grounds: (1) the sole entry language requirement is English B2, with no second or third language required at entry; (2) there is NO exit/graduation language requirement — unibz's own language-model page for English-taught masters states 'even if your Master's programme is entirely in English and does not include language requirements in other languages, you can certainly attend the Language Centre's language courses to improve your language skills or learn a new language', confirming that Italian/German study is optional enrichment, not an obligation; (3) the admission-information PDF's language section lists only an 'Entry level (to gain admission): English: B2' row and contains no 'Exit level' row at all — whereas the trilingual bachelor's PDF lists both entry (B2/B2/none) and exit (C1/C1/B2) levels; (4) empirical proof from the published ranking lists: 30 of 30 non-EU places were filled in the Early Bird session with a further 15 applicants on the waiting list, and only 2 EU applicants in that session were excluded on language grounds — i.e. the language gate is a low, single-language hurdle that the overwhelming majority clear, not the mass-exclusion filter seen in the trilingual bachelor. For a Turkish applicant with English only, this programme is one of the most accessible at unibz. The binding constraint here is competition and academic prerequisites, not language.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list, decided by documentary evaluation of the applicant's study career. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO CENT-S, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter and NO video. The distinguishing instrument is a CONDITIONAL ONLINE INTERVIEW, triggered only for applicants whose bachelor grade average is below 24/30. Selection therefore has three gates: (a) an eliminatory prerequisite gate — the admission title plus curricular ECTS/SSD requirements plus English B2, none of which score points; (b) for sub-24/30 applicants only, a pass/fail online interview; (c) a scored ranking on grade average (up to 10 points) plus a Webometrics university-ranking bonus (up to 3 points). Separate ranking lists are drawn for (i) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (ii) non-EU citizens living abroad, each against its own quota.
academic_requirements: TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES TO THE ADMISSION TITLE. Route A — a bachelor's degree in Computer Science (Italian class L-31) or Information Engineering (Italian class L-08), or an equivalent qualification under previous Italian regulations, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad; unibz names as examples: Computer Science, Software Engineering, Business Informatics, Information Engineering. Route B — a bachelor's degree in ANY discipline, provided the following curricular requirements have been obtained through bachelor's degrees, master's degrees or single subject courses: AT LEAST 12 ECTS in the computer-science group, and AT LEAST 12 ECTS in the mathematics/statistics/physics group. COMPUTER SCIENCE GROUP (new 2024-reform SSD codes with old equivalents): INFO-01/A (ex INF/01) Computer Science; IINF-05/A (ex ING-INF/05) Information Processing Systems. MATHEMATICS/STATISTICS/PHYSICS GROUP: MATH-01/A (ex MAT/01) Mathematical Logic; MATH-02/A (ex MAT/02) Algebra; MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03) Geometry; MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05) Mathematical Analysis; MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06) Mathematical Probability and Statistics; MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07) Mathematical Physics; MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08) Numerical Analysis; MATH-06/A (ex MAT/09) Operational Research; STAT-01/A (ex SECS-S/01) Statistics; STAT-01/B (ex SECS-S/02) Statistics for Experimental and Technological Research; STAT-02/A (ex SECS-S/03) Economic Statistics; PHYS-01/A (ex FIS/01 and FIS/04) Experimental Physics of Fundamental Interactions and Applications; PHYS-02/A (ex FIS/02 and FIS/04) Theoretical Physics of Fundamental Interactions, Models, Mathematical Methods and Applications; PHYS-03/A (ex FIS/01 and FIS/03) Experimental Physics of Matter and Applications; PHYS-04/A (ex FIS/02 and FIS/03) Theoretical Physics of Matter, Models, Mathematical Methods and Applications. FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: 'For candidates with a qualification obtained abroad the verification of the curricular requirements is based on the specific contents of the educational activities' — i.e. unibz maps course CONTENT, not SSD labels (Turkish and other non-Italian transcripts carry no SSD codes), which is precisely why the study-career Excel file demands the courses be sorted by disciplinary area. GRADE THRESHOLD: candidates must have an average mark of at least 24/30; those below must pass the online interview. DEGREE VOLUME: at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must show at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Crucially, possession of the curricular requirements 'does not give a score but is an admission prerequisite' — meeting them earns nothing, failing them excludes. NATIONAL RULE: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed, but they must not belong to the same class (not LM-18/LM-18) and must differ in at least 2/3 of course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance examination of any kind — no unibz aptitude test, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT requirement. The only assessment instruments connected to admission are: (1) the CONDITIONAL ONLINE INTERVIEW in English, required only of candidates whose bachelor average is below 24/30 (see the 'interview' field for dates and subject matter); (2) LANGUAGE EXAMS at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who choose that route to prove English B2 rather than submitting a certificate or a prior English-medium qualification — Early Bird sessions 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026; this date was subsequently marked fully booked) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late session 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Applicants in the Additional Application Session CANNOT use unibz language exams and must submit a language certificate instead. Separately and not part of selection, a non-compulsory Mathematics pre-course runs 21/09-09/10/2026 for admitted students.
selection_scoring: Maximum 13 points, awarded on documents only. (1) ADMISSION TITLE — up to 10 points, 'based on the grade average obtained at the time of application'. (2) STUDY CURRICULUM / WEBOMETRICS BONUS — the score for the study curriculum is weighted on the 'Webometrics Ranking of World Universities': 3 points for universities ranked 1-1000; 2 points for 1001-2000; 1 point for 2001-3000; 0 points for 3001 onwards. (3) Curricular requirements — no score, admission prerequisite only. (4) English proficiency certificate — no score, admission prerequisite only. ELIMINATORY THRESHOLD: an average mark of at least 24/30; candidates below it are not excluded outright but must pass the online interview to remain in the procedure. No overall minimum total score is published, and no tie-break rule is published for this programme. COMPETITION LEVEL 2026/27 (from the signed ranking lists) — sharply asymmetric: EU/parity applicants were UNDER-subscribed (17 admitted against 20 Early Bird places; 7 admitted in the Late session), so a qualifying EU-status applicant was essentially certain of a place. Non-EU applicants living abroad were OVER-subscribed: all 30 places filled and a further 15 applicants (ranks 31-45) placed on a waiting list, i.e. at least 45 fully eligible non-EU candidates competed for 30 places. The practical implication is that for a non-EU applicant the Webometrics bonus and the grade average genuinely decide the outcome, whereas for an EU/parity applicant they barely matter.
bonus_points: One bonus mechanism only: the WEBOMETRICS RANKING OF WORLD UNIVERSITIES bonus attached to the applicant's previous university — 3 points for a university ranked 1 to 1000, 2 points for 1001-2000, 1 point for 2001-3000, and 0 points from 3001 onwards. This is worth up to 3 of the 13 available points (roughly 23% of the maximum) and is the only lever an applicant cannot influence at application time. The same mechanism is used by the sister Master in Software Engineering. There is NO GMAT/GRE bonus (that belongs to the Master in Accounting and Finance), NO startup-project bonus (Entrepreneurship), and NO extracurricular-activities bonus (that is the bachelor-level mechanism). Practical note for applicants: because the study-career Excel file requires the university's website to be declared, unibz looks the institution up in Webometrics itself; most established Turkish state universities fall in the 1001-3000 band, i.e. 1-2 points, while a handful reach the top 1000.
portfolio_and_materials: NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video, NO project proposal, NO reference letters, NO CV are required — none of these instruments are used by this programme, and no file-size or page limits exist because there is nothing of that kind to submit. The one mandatory STRUCTURED upload is the STUDY CAREER EXCEL FILE, which is this programme's equivalent of a portfolio and is the single most error-prone part of the application. Rules, taken from the template's own guidelines: download the .xlsx template and the PDF example of a filled-in file from the application portal; fill in BOTH worksheets — tab 'ADMISSION TITLE (BACHELOR)' for the bachelor degree and tab 'OTHER UNIVERSITY COURSES' for anything else (master courses, single subject courses); save the file as surname-name.xls; and 'Upload the .xls file (not a PDF version of it)'. Content rules: do not change the structure of the file, only add rows; indicate the AVERAGE MARK plus the minimum pass grade and maximum grade; if a FINAL GRADE (voto di laurea, GPA or CGPA) exists you MUST state it together with its minimum and maximum thresholds; insert ALL courses taken during the bachelor; divide courses by disciplinary area exactly as labelled in the template ('AREA: COMPUTER SCIENCE', 'AREA: MATHEMATICS', 'AREA: STATISTICS', 'AREA: PHYSICS', 'Other disciplines'); state the SSD only for courses taken at an Italian university; use your LOCAL credits, not converted ECTS; if two grading scales are used (e.g. theory vs labs) declare both and tag each course 'GS 1' or 'GS 2'; for the second tab also give total class hours and the awarding university with town and country; do not duplicate in the second tab courses already listed in the first. Template file: /assets/Documents/Faculty-Computer-Science/2026-02-24-Master-in-Computing-for-Data-Science-to-fill-out-by-the-student.xlsx ; worked example: /assets/Documents/Faculty-Computer-Science/2025-02-24-Master-in-Computing-for-Data-Science-admission-procedure.pdf (a filled specimen for a fictitious 'Bruce Wayne'). Failure to supply this correctly is an exclusion, not a deduction: 'If you graduated in Italy, you must self-declare the exams passed, otherwise you will be excluded. If you graduated abroad, you must upload your academic transcript, otherwise you will be excluded.'
interview: YES — a conditional online interview, and it is genuinely enforced. Trigger: only candidates whose bachelor grade average is BELOW 24/30. Format: an online interview held in English in which the candidate must 'demonstrate their knowledge in topics such as Programming Languages and Paradigms, Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Management Systems, Linear Algebra, Probability Theory' — i.e. a technical competence check, not a motivational chat. It is pass/fail and does not add points to the ranking. PUBLISHED DATES for 2026/27: Early Bird Application — 22/05/2026 and 26/05/2026 (2026-05-22 and 2026-05-26); Late Application — 28-29/07/2026 (2026-07-28 to 2026-07-29); Additional Application Session — 17/09/2026 (2026-09-17). Enforcement evidence: the signed Late Application ranking list contains a dedicated exclusion category, 'The following persons did not attend the interviews and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure', naming 2 applicant IDs — non-attendance is an automatic exclusion. Candidates at or above 24/30 are not interviewed at all.
conditional_admission: Two distinct conditional regimes, both explicitly documented. (1) NOT YET GRADUATED — 'You can apply if you have acquired at least 120 credit points (ECTS). In this case you will be admitted conditionally submitting your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The threshold for this programme is 120 ECTS (not the 140 used by Data Analytics). The ranking lists repeat: 'Applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday).' If the degree is obtained AFTER the enrolment deadline the place is lost and passes to the next applicant; unibz gives explicit financial advice: 'If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place.' A late enrolment request may then be submitted to the Rector and, ONLY if places are still available, enrolment is possible by 11 DECEMBER 2026 (2026-12-11). (2) ADMISSION WITH RESERVATION for foreign qualifications — 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified'; the reservation is lifted once ARDI/CIMEA documents are uploaded and the title is deemed eligible, otherwise enrolment is refused. A further warning applies even after enrolment: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' (3) A THIRD, non-EU-specific conditionality appears in the Early Bird ranking list: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.'
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — no OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) mechanism exists for this programme. OFA is an undergraduate instrument at unibz, used for the economics bachelors (mathematics test) and the Bachelor in Computer Science (mathematics grade average). At master level the equivalent quality gate is handled entirely before admission, through the eliminatory curricular ECTS/SSD requirements and, for sub-24/30 candidates, the online interview. Neither the admission-information PDF nor either signed ranking list mentions OFA, and no ranking entries carry the OFA asterisk used in the bachelor lists. The Mathematics pre-course (21/09-09/10/2026) is a voluntary preparatory offering, not an OFA remedy.
language_requirements: Single-language regime, and by unibz standards a light one. 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) — English: B2.' CEFR levels apply. No Italian, no German, no second or third language is required at any point, at entry or at graduation. Proof must be provided in the application portal (sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams') AFTER creating an application in 'create/manage applications'. Administrative distinction: a final certificate awarded by an ITALIAN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a FOREIGN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma. The language check is eliminatory but shallow: in the 2026/27 Early Bird session only 2 EU applicants were excluded for language and in the Late session only 1 — a very different picture from the trilingual bachelor, where dozens were excluded. Optional enrichment: Language Centre courses in German, Italian and other languages are free and open to these students, and intensive courses run 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day), but attendance carries no academic obligation for this programme.
entry_levels_by_position: NOT APPLICABLE in the unibz 1st/2nd/3rd-language-position sense — that framework governs only the trilingual programmes. This programme has a single language position: English at B2. Expressed in the schema's notation the pattern is B2 / none / none. There is no 'strongest-language' ranking to declare, no second-language certification, and no third language. For comparison within the same faculty: Bachelor in Computer Science is B2/B2/none, Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none, Public Policy and Accounting and Finance C1/B2/none — this master sits well below all of them in language burden. Note that unibz Language Centre exams can only be registered at B2 level, which exactly matches the level this programme needs.
exit_levels: NONE — there is no language requirement to graduate. This is an unusual and highly consequential finding, so it rests on three independent supports: (1) the admission-information PDF's language section contains an 'Entry level (to gain admission)' heading and no 'Exit level (to graduate)' heading at all, whereas the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science PDF carries both; (2) the official study plan's 'Teaching language' section says only 'The official language of the Master's programme is English', with no graduation language clause; (3) unibz's language-model page dedicated to English-taught master programmes states that such a programme 'is entirely in English and does not include language requirements in other languages'. A student therefore graduates without ever certifying Italian or German. The only language-adjacent graduation element is the compulsory 3 CP pass/fail course 'Advanced English for Scientific Communication' in year 2 semester 2, which is an academic-writing and scientific-communication course taken in English, not a CEFR certification.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE. The B1-in-the-third-language rule that gates curricular examinations in the trilingual programmes does not exist here, because there is no second or third language in the study plan. Every examination in this programme is held in English, so the single English B2 entry requirement is sufficient to sit every exam from day one. There is likewise no third-language placement test for admitted students and no obligation to reach B1 by mid-January (that clause exists for trilingual students whose third language is English — the mirror image of this programme's situation).
proof_pathways: Four recognised ways to prove English B2, all handled inside the application portal. (1) MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH-SCHOOL YEAR, if English — recognised as C1. For foreign qualifications: 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE IN ENGLISH — recognised as C1. unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1). For foreign qualifications: 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' This is the most common route for applicants from English-medium engineering faculties, including many Turkish universities, but note that a supporting letter from the university is required whenever the degree certificate itself is silent on the medium of instruction. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list. 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' Common B2 thresholds from the official list: IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5-6.5; TOEFL iBT 72-94; PTE Academic 59-75; Pearson English International Certificate B2; PTE General Level 3; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, or B2 First for Schools grade B or C, or B1 Preliminary (PET) grade A, or B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage); LanguageCert General B2 / LanguageCert Academic; Aptis ESOL Advanced B2; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; MET B1-level entries map lower — check the table. Anything at C1 or C2 obviously also satisfies B2. (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered online through the portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out the application — Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026; later shown as fully booked) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Important sequencing trap: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Applicants in the Additional Application Session cannot use route 4 and must rely on routes 1-3.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'. General dispositions, quoted from the English column of the trilingual resolution: a certificate must (1) 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and (2) 'indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation)'. Further rules: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed' — the weakest sub-skill sets the level; 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation'; 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list'; 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted' — you cannot assemble a certificate from multiple providers; 'Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised'; 'Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised'; 'DAAD certificates are not recognised'. VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' — i.e. certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year remain valid for the whole of the current year. Items in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section have unlimited validity. [uncertain] — the home-edition exception: in the extracted table an asterisk defined as 'Also accepted as "home edition"' appears against several major tests including IELTS, TOEFL and TOEIC, which would mean their at-home variants ARE accepted; because this asterisk is rendered from a complex multi-column PDF table its exact scope could not be confirmed cell by cell, so an applicant relying on an at-home test should verify with language.centre@unibz.it before applying. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). All deadlines fall at NOON local time, not midnight. EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only if places remain): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04 — and this session IS confirmed open for this programme on the official Additional Application Session page, marked '(Application possible)'. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second. As of the 2026-08-29 verification date the Early Bird and Late sessions have closed with ranking lists published; only the Additional Session window remains open, and it closes 2026-09-04 at noon.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. The admission-information PDF is explicit: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or for the Additional Application Session — both are labelled 'only for EU citizens'. They are ranked on a separate list against the separate 30-place non-EU quota and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: for a Turkish applicant without an Italian residence permit there is exactly one shot per academic year, closing at the end of April — roughly five months before teaching starts. Missing it means waiting a full year.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants, and the second is the critical one for Turkish and other non-EU nationals already in Italy. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay.' Explicit exclusion: 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' If the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The ranking list restates this: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy ... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' WHY THIS MATTERS ENORMOUSLY FOR THIS PROGRAMME: the two pools had opposite competitive dynamics in 2026/27 — the EU/parity pool was under-subscribed (17 admitted against 20 Early Bird places, 7 in the Late session) while the non-EU pool was full with a 15-person waiting list. A qualifying applicant who fails to upload the permit therefore moves from a near-certain admission into the most competitive pool in the programme, and simultaneously loses access to the Late and Additional sessions.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27, and this programme's non-EU allocation is unusually generous by unibz standards. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 20 places; Late Application 10 places; total 30. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 30 places; no non-EU quota in any later session. The brochure and programme page summarise this as 'Places available: 30 EU + 30 non-EU' (30 = 20 + 10), so a 1:1 EU-to-non-EU ratio — compare the sister Bachelor in Computer Science at 50 EU + 4 non-EU. CARRY-OVER RULE: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application' — the carry-over benefits EU applicants only, and unfilled EU places are never transferred to the non-EU pool. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE from the signed ranking lists: Early Bird — 17 EU/parity admitted (against 20), 30 non-EU admitted (exactly filling 30) plus 15 on the waiting list at ranks 31-45; Late — 7 EU/parity admitted. Total admitted across both sessions: 24 EU/parity and 30 non-EU. So the non-EU quota was fully consumed and over-subscribed by at least 50%, while the EU quota went 6 places short — which is why the Additional Application Session was opened for this programme.

required_documents: AT APPLICATION, via the portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ : (1) a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed online form; (3) THE STUDY CAREER EXCEL FILE — both worksheets ('Admission title' and 'Other university courses') filled in and uploaded AS AN EXCEL FILE, not as a PDF (the mandatory structured upload for this programme; see portfolio_and_materials for the full rules); (4) for graduates of Italian universities, self-declaration of the exams passed — 'otherwise you will be excluded'; (5) for graduates abroad, the ACADEMIC TRANSCRIPT — 'otherwise you will be excluded'; (6) proof of English B2, uploaded under 'upload language certificates' or registration for a Language Centre exam under 'enrol for language exams'; (7) if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (8) for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay, plus a renewal request if it has expired. Once submitted the application CANNOT be modified, and 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the degree diploma of the Bachelor; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English); and the DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT, which must indicate both that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Then, depending on the education system, the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements (see credential_recognition). Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. Stated in the admission-information PDF as: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' In the parallel bachelor documentation unibz describes the same charge as an administration fee that is explicitly non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay NO application fee. This is a further concrete advantage of establishing parity of treatment where genuinely available.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, paid in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which 'includes the revenue stamp of € 16' (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, 'must be paid by March of the following year'. 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992, or with a disability of 66% or more (the disability certificate from the health authorities must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year); and foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students who receive a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano 'are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees'. At roughly €1,200 per year the programme is inexpensive by international-master standards, and the fee is identical for EU and non-EU students — there is no differentiated international tuition rate. Reference pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the admission-information PDF https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-computing-for-data-science_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for the Right to Study / Office for Higher Education Support and applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. The province offers three instruments: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant holders also receive a refund of the tuition fees paid: 'If you are able to receive a grant from the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, you receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year.' CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS, quoted verbatim: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' A newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively ineligible in year one and can realistically only access the grant from year two — which for a two-year master means at most one funded year. Other listed funding sources: Italian government grants (applied for via Italian embassies/consulates, and which also carry full tuition exemption), Austrian student grants, German BAföG, DAAD summer-course scholarships, and Italian bank study loans. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships. No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Master in Computing for Data Science. [uncertain] — the grant range of roughly €1,680-€6,960 per year and any merit threshold such as a 27/30 average after the first year could not be confirmed on any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually and should be checked directly. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the Bachelor degree diploma, an official translation into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English), and the Diploma Supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — a Statement of Correspondence of the Bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE NOT SIGNATORIES OF THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' Exclusion by Rector's decree remains possible even after enrolment if the title turns out to be invalid. TÜRKİYE is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification — note this is a two-document requirement and CIMEA verification takes time and carries a fee, so it should be started well before the October enrolment deadline. Separately, the curricular-requirements check at APPLICATION stage is done by unibz itself on course content, not by CIMEA: 'For candidates with a qualification obtained abroad the verification of the curricular requirements is based on the specific contents of the educational activities.' Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses. Links: https://ardi.cimea.it/en ; https://cimea-diplome.it/page-comparability-verification-service ; https://cimea-diplome.it/page-verification-service ; signatory list https://www.enic-naric.net/
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window ONLY (02/03-28/04/2026, €50 fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (30 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application by pre-enrolling on the Universitaly portal. The Universitaly application is MANDATORY: 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and the ranking list is blunter — 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' Only ONE study programme may be selected on Universitaly. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. EXPLICIT CAVEATS: 'preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates', 'the application at unibz does not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation', and 'obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme'. FINANCIAL MEANS for the visa: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area, and a total of €24,000 for a MASTER programme (the bachelor figure is €36,000) — this reflects the two-year duration. Health insurance and visa expenses must also be budgeted. A further non-EU-specific admission condition appears in the ranking list: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' AFTER ARRIVAL: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service / Student Support immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country ARE entitled to a refund — the only refund exception for this programme. Universitaly: https://www.universitaly.it/

uncertainty_notes: DATA YEAR: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 03.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change.' Verified as of 2026-08-29. TIMING STATUS AT VERIFICATION: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 have CLOSED and both signed ranking lists are published; the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION IS OPEN for this programme (18/08-04/09/2026 noon, EU citizens and parity-of-treatment applicants only) and closes within days of the verification date — this is time-critical and should be re-checked before any use. (1) RESOLVED CONFLICT ON PLACES: an automated first pass over the programme page's HTML reported EU places as '30 Early Bird + 10 Late'. That is WRONG. Both the raw HTML page text and the admission-information PDF state 'Early Bird Application: 20, Late Application: 10' for EU and 'Early Bird Application: 30' for non-EU; the brochure's summary '30 EU + 30 non-EU' reconciles with 20+10=30. The 20/10/30 split is authoritative. (2) PDF SLUG TRAP: the admission-information and brochure PDFs live under the slug 'master-in-computing-for-data-science' (with 'for'), while the programme page URL uses 'master-computing-data-science' (without 'for'). Deriving the PDF path from the page slug produces a 404. (3) PREDECESSOR PROGRAMME: the researcher's working note that this replaces a closed MSc Computer Science is SUPPORTED but with a nuance — unibz never says 'closed'; the study-guide page says pre-2021/22 students are enrolled in 'our previous Master in Computer Science or in a previous version of our Master in Computational Data Science' and urges them to switch. So the current programme is the successor to two predecessors, restructured from 2021/22, and the archived manifestos on the site are those of the old MSc CS. No unibz page states an explicit closure date for the old programme. (4) NON-EU QUOTA: the working note that the non-EU quota is 'unusually high (30)' is CONFIRMED and is arguably the single most useful fact about this programme — a 1:1 EU:non-EU ratio, versus 50:4 at the sister Bachelor in Computer Science. But the 2026/27 outcome shows that quota was fully consumed with 15 more on the waiting list, so a generous quota does not mean easy entry for non-EU applicants; it means the opposite of the EU picture. (5) NO EXIT LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT: this is asserted from the structural absence of an 'Exit level' section in the admission PDF combined with the affirmative statement on the English-taught-masters language-model page. No page states 'there is no exit requirement' in those words, so the conclusion is inferential, though strongly supported by three independent sources. (6) CERTIFICATE HOME-EDITION SCOPE: flagged inline — the asterisk marking 'Also accepted as home edition' appears against several major tests (IELTS, TOEFL, TOEIC) in the extracted table, but multi-column PDF table extraction cannot confirm the asterisk's exact per-cell scope; verify with language.centre@unibz.it before relying on an at-home test. (7) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS: the €1,680-€6,960 range and any 27/30 merit threshold in the field schema could not be confirmed on any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually. (8) NO OFA, NO PORTFOLIO, NO TOLC/SAT/CENT-S, NO GMAT/GRE BONUS for this programme — these schema fields are populated with explicit not-applicable findings rather than left empty, to avoid a later reader inferring 'unknown'. (9) NO PUBLISHED TIE-BREAK RULE and no published minimum total score; the bachelor-level 'younger applicant wins' tie-break is not stated for this master. (10) The Additional Session ranking list (due by 18/09/2026) did not exist at verification, so its outcome and the exact number of remaining places are unknown; the EU shortfall of 6 places (24 admitted against 30) is the best available estimate of capacity. (11) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE: Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so case (b) recognition applies (ARDI + CIMEA Verification) — this classification is inferred from convention membership, not stated by unibz for this programme.
